finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml::mutable `@v1` tag for the action that consumes agent_app_private_key, in the same job as the sha-pinned claude-code-action step
evidence: The code fact checks out: in the supplied .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml the "Generate GitHub App token" step is `uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v1` (mutable tag) receiving `secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, while the claude-code-action step in the same job is SHA-pinned with an explicit supply-chain comment — so the described asymmetry is actually present, though on lines the diff does not touch (the diff only adds `allowed_bots` and extends `stalled`'s needs/if). The claim's justification is largely wrong, however: it says every other App-token site pins a SHA, but agent-review-panel.yml at this commit also uses plain `actions/create-github-app-token@v1`, and the cited agent-fix.yml/agent-rerun.yml/agent-loop.yml/agent-summarize.yml/agent-review-on-demand.yml do not exist at this revision; all cited line numbers are off by 35–120 lines, suggesting the finding was written against a different tree. I rate it minor rather than major: `actions/create-github-app-token` is a first-party GitHub action, floating its major tag is common accepted practice, the repo does this uniformly (so there is no self-inconsistency to fix here specifically), and the condition is pre-existing rather than introduced. Confidence is medium because I could only read the two supplied workflow files and not the withheld/absent ones the claim leans on.
